---
title: "Raster Band Math: Combining Two Bands Into One"
date: 2026-09-07
categories: [tool, raster, bilingual]
description: "Pick two bands, an operation, and get a computed raster back — as a colored map and a downloadable GeoTIFF — in Python and R on the same map."
---

A single band answers one question per pixel — elevation, reflectance
in one wavelength, a single sensor reading. Most useful raster
questions need two: how much did this change between two dates, how
different is band A from band B, is this pixel more one thing than
another. Band math is the term for exactly that — pixel-by-pixel
arithmetic between two bands of the same raster, producing a new
single-band raster the same size as the inputs.

Just want the computed result, without the rest of the reading? Use
the [standalone tool](/tools/raster-calculator.html) — same engine,
pick your bands and operator directly.

## 1. Upload your file

A single `.tif`/`.tiff` with two or more bands — band math has
nothing to compute on a single-band file.

## 2. Why band math?

Four things worth knowing before the first computed raster:

- **It's pixel-by-pixel, not band-by-band.** Every output pixel comes
  from exactly the two input pixels at the same row/column — a
  computed raster is always the same width, height, and (usually)
  resolution as its inputs, never a summary or a reduction.
- **NoData has to propagate, not get treated as a real number.** If
  either input pixel is NoData, the output pixel has to be NoData too
  — otherwise a border of sentinel values (often `-9999` or `0`) quietly
  drags a mean or a color ramp toward a value that was never a real
  measurement.
- **Division needs a plan for zero.** `A ÷ B` on a pixel where `B` is
  `0` isn't a crash waiting to happen — it's `Inf` (or `NaN` for `0 ÷ 0`)
  in both Python and R, and both are just as "not a real value" as
  NoData is. Left unhandled, a single such pixel can make an entire
  color ramp or `min`/`max` computation meaningless.
- **A very common form has a name**: `(A − B) / (A + B)` —
  *Normalized Difference* — bounds the result to roughly `-1..1`
  regardless of the two bands' original units, which is exactly why
  it shows up everywhere from vegetation indices to change detection.
  This article computes a plain difference (`A − B`) as the running
  example; try changing the formula in the code below to see how the
  normalized form differs.

```{ojs}
  await map.ready();
  return map;
}
```

```{ojs}
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// base64 -> raw bytes, same pattern as the CRS Inspector/Validator's
// binary downloads — here decoding computed float32 pixels instead of
// a zip file.
base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
  const binary = atob(base64Str);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same reasoning as raster-file-inspection.qmd's pySummary/rSummary:
// separate mutable state so Reset can clear the cards even though
// there's nothing to re-run.
mutable pyResult = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable rResult = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
pyCompute = WebGeoDS.getCellValue("bandmath-py", Generators)
{
  if (pyCompute && pyCompute.summary) {
    const s = pyCompute.summary;
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("bandmath-py-footprint", pyCompute.footprint, { paint: FOOTPRINT_PAINT });
    await sharedMap.fitToData(pyCompute.footprint);
    if (s.min !== null) {
      await sharedMap.setRasterImage("bandmath-py-result", {
        bounds: s.wgs84Bounds,
        width: s.width,
        height: s.height,
        values: new Float32Array(base64ToBytes(s.data).buffer),
        min: s.min,
        max: s.max
      });
    }
    mutable pyResult = s;
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Two cards side by side, same reasoning as the Inspector article: a
// combined number wouldn't mean anything, but seeing the two engines'
// results agree (or noticing where they don't) is itself the point —
// see section 5.
statCard = (label, s) => {
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.style.flex = "1";
  wrap.style.minWidth = "260px";

  const heading = document.createElement("div");
  heading.className = "webgeods-label";
  heading.textContent = label;
  wrap.appendChild(heading);

  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";
  wrap.appendChild(box);

  const row = (rowLabel, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = rowLabel;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s) {
    row("Result", "—");
    return wrap;
  }

  row("Dimensions", `${s.width} × ${s.height} px`);
  row("CRS", s.crs === null || s.crs === undefined ? `Unknown ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : s.crs);
  if (s.displayCrsAssumption) {
    row("Display assumption", `${s.displayCrsAssumption} — map only, not a fact about the file`);
  }
  row("Output range", s.min !== null ? `${s.min} to ${s.max} (mean ${s.mean})` : "all NoData");
  row("NoData pixels", `${s.nodataCount.toLocaleString()} / ${s.totalPixels.toLocaleString()}`);

  return wrap;
}
```

## 4. Compute: run the same band math in Python or R

Run the same computation on the current data (your file uploaded
above, or the built-in example below) — edit `band_a`/`band_b`, or the
formula itself, and re-run to see the map update.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Python

```{.webgeods-python #bandmath-py}
#| package: rasterio, numpy
import base64
import rasterio
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from rasterio.io import MemoryFile
from rasterio.warp import transform_bounds
import numpy as np

path = None
for candidate in ["/uploaded.tif"]:
    try:
        with rasterio.open(candidate):
            path = candidate
            break
    except Exception:
        pass

# No file uploaded yet: two small synthetic hills built directly in
# memory, close enough together that A - B is a non-trivial pattern
# rather than ~0 everywhere.
memfile = None
if path is None:
    n = 20
    xs = np.arange(n)
    ys = np.arange(n)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    band1 = (100 + 40 * np.exp(-((X - 10) ** 2 + (Y - 10) ** 2) / 30)).astype("float32")
    band2 = (100 + 25 * np.exp(-((X - 6) ** 2 + (Y - 14) ** 2) / 40)).astype("float32")
    band1[0, 0] = -9999
    band2[0, 0] = -9999
    transform = from_origin(12.40, 41.95, 0.005, 0.005)
    memfile = MemoryFile()
    with memfile.open(
        driver="GTiff", height=n, width=n, count=2,
        dtype="float32", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=transform, nodata=-9999
    ) as dst:
        dst.write(band1, 1)
        dst.write(band2, 2)
    path = memfile.name

band_a = 1
band_b = 2

with rasterio.open(path) as src:
    a = src.read(band_a, masked=True).astype("float32").filled(np.nan)
    b = src.read(band_b, masked=True).astype("float32").filled(np.nan)

    # Plain difference — try (a - b) / (a + b) (Normalized Difference)
    # instead, and re-run, to see how the result and its color range
    # change.
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        result = a - b

    # Inf/NaN (from a formula that divides, on a zero pixel) folded
    # into NoData the same way — the map/legend/stats below only ever
    # have to reason about "finite" vs "not".
    result[~np.isfinite(result)] = np.nan

    valid = result[np.isfinite(result)]
    has_valid = valid.size > 0

    # Same missing-CRS convention as the other Raster tools: unknown
    # stays unknown in "crs", never silently relabeled as WGS84.
    crs_warning = None
    display_crs_assumption = None
    if src.crs is not None:
        crs_for_transform = src.crs
        crs_label = str(src.crs)
    else:
        crs_for_transform = "EPSG:4326"
        crs_label = None
        crs_warning = "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
        display_crs_assumption = "EPSG:4326"

    try:
        wgs84_bounds = transform_bounds(crs_for_transform, "EPSG:4326", *src.bounds)
    except Exception:
        wgs84_bounds = src.bounds

    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = wgs84_bounds
    footprint = {
        "type": "FeatureCollection",
        "features": [{
            "type": "Feature",
            "properties": {"name": "band math footprint"},
            "geometry": {
                "type": "Polygon",
                "coordinates": [[[minx, miny], [maxx, miny], [maxx, maxy], [minx, maxy], [minx, miny]]]
            }
        }]
    }

    data_b64 = base64.b64encode(result.astype("float32").tobytes()).decode("ascii")

    summary = {
        "width": src.width,
        "height": src.height,
        "data": data_b64,
        "wgs84Bounds": [round(float(v), 6) for v in wgs84_bounds],
        "crs": crs_label,
        "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "displayCrsAssumption": display_crs_assumption,
        "min": round(float(valid.min()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        "max": round(float(valid.max()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        "mean": round(float(valid.mean()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        "nodataCount": int(result.size - valid.size),
        "totalPixels": int(result.size),
    }

if memfile is not None:
    memfile.close()

{
    "summary": summary,
    "footprint": footprint
}
```

## R

```{.webgeods-r #bandmath-r}
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

if (is.null(path)) {
  # Same synthetic pair as the Python fallback.
  n <- 20
  xs <- 0:(n - 1)
  ys <- 0:(n - 1)
  band1 <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
  band2 <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 25 * exp(-((x - 6)^2 + (y - 14)^2) / 40))
  band1[1, 1] <- NA
  band2[1, 1] <- NA
  r <- c(
    rast(band1, crs = "EPSG:4326"),
    rast(band2, crs = "EPSG:4326")
  )
  ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)
} else {
  r <- rast(path)
}

band_a <- 1
band_b <- 2

a <- r[[band_a]]
b <- r[[band_b]]

# Plain difference — try (a - b) / (a + b) (Normalized Difference)
# instead, and re-run.
result <- a - b

# terra's SpatRaster supports Ops/Math group generics directly, so
# is.finite() works elementwise here exactly like it does on a plain
# numeric vector; ifel() is terra's own vectorized if/else, replacing
# every non-finite cell (from a divide, if you try Normalized
# Difference above) with NA — same reasoning as the Python cell's
# np.errstate + isfinite mask.
result <- ifel(is.finite(result), result, NA)

# Same missing-CRS convention as the Python side. terra reports a
# missing CRS as an empty string, not NA.
was_missing_crs <- crs(r) == ""
crs_warning <- NULL
display_crs_assumption <- NULL
if (was_missing_crs) {
  crs_warning <- "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
  display_crs_assumption <- "EPSG:4326"
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
}
crs_label <- if (was_missing_crs) {
  NULL
} else {
  crs_desc <- crs(r, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(r, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

e <- ext(r)
bounds <- c(e$xmin, e$ymin, e$xmax, e$ymax)

bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
  e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(r))
bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))
e_wgs84 <- ext(bbox_wgs84)

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("band math footprint")),
    geometry = list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"),
      coordinates = list(footprint_coords)
    )
  ))
)

# Row-major flat vector, same cell order terra itself reads/writes a
# raster in (matches rasterio's own row-major convention on the
# Python side) -- values(mat = FALSE) returns exactly that order.
vals <- values(result, mat = FALSE)
valid <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
has_valid <- length(valid) > 0

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(as.numeric(ifelse(is.finite(vals), vals, NaN)), con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
data_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

# jsonlite::toJSON() treats every length-1 vector as a single-element
# array by default — a genuine scalar (a width, a CRS string) needs an
# explicit jsonlite::unbox() to serialize as one. ub()/ub_if() below
# are just that, plus a NULL passthrough for optional fields (see
# geospatial-file-inspection.qmd for the full reasoning on why this,
# not toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE), is the safer default).
ub <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(x)
ub_if <- function(cond, x) if (cond) jsonlite::unbox(x) else NULL

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
  height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
  data = jsonlite::unbox(data_b64),
  wgs84Bounds = round(c(e_wgs84$xmin, e_wgs84$ymin, e_wgs84$xmax, e_wgs84$ymax), 6),
  crs = ub(crs_label),
  crsWarning = ub(crs_warning),
  displayCrsAssumption = ub(display_crs_assumption),
  min = ub_if(has_valid, round(min(valid), 4)),
  max = ub_if(has_valid, round(max(valid), 4)),
  mean = ub_if(has_valid, round(mean(valid), 4)),
  nodataCount = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals) - length(valid)),
  totalPixels = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals))
)

result_out <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

:::

## 5. Same spatial question, two languages

Both engines agree on the arithmetic itself (elementwise subtraction
is elementwise subtraction), but differ in how NoData and
non-finite results are handled:

**Python** (rasterio + numpy)

```python
src.read(i, masked=True).astype("float32").filled(np.nan)  # NoData -> NaN up front
a - b                                                        # plain numpy arithmetic
result[~np.isfinite(result)] = np.nan                        # Inf/NaN from division -> NaN
```

**R** (terra)

```r
r[[i]]                              # one band as its own SpatRaster
a - b                                # terra overloads +-*/ directly on SpatRaster
ifel(is.finite(result), result, NA)  # Inf/NaN from division -> NA
```

The shape of the fix is identical in both languages — mask out
non-finite values after the arithmetic, don't try to prevent them
from occurring — but the *mechanism* differs: numpy needs an explicit
`np.errstate` context to suppress the runtime warning a division by
zero would otherwise print (the computation itself still produces
`Inf`/`NaN` either way), while terra's `ifel()` is a single vectorized
call with no equivalent warning to suppress.

## 6. A raster with no declared CRS

The reusable cell pair above already builds two small synthetic hills
whenever nothing has been uploaded — click **▶ Run** on both languages
in section 4 to see it. This button swaps in the same pair, minus the
CRS, to see the CRS row switch to "Unknown" and a separate "Display
assumption" row appear below it — same convention as every other
Raster tool on this site.[^bandmath-crs-missing]

[^bandmath-crs-missing]: Band math doesn't change anything about this
— the two input bands either both carry a real CRS or don't, and the
computed output inherits whichever is true. A missing CRS says
nothing about whether the arithmetic itself is trustworthy, only about
where the result sits on the earth.


```{ojs}
//| echo: false

rNoCrsExampleCode = `library(terra)

n <- 20
xs <- 0:(n - 1)
ys <- 0:(n - 1)
band1 <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
band2 <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 25 * exp(-((x - 6)^2 + (y - 14)^2) / 40))
band1[1, 1] <- NA
band2[1, 1] <- NA
# crs deliberately omitted from rast() -- the whole point of this example.
r <- c(rast(band1), rast(band2))
ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)

band_a <- 1
band_b <- 2
a <- r[[band_a]]
b <- r[[band_b]]
result <- a - b
result <- ifel(is.finite(result), result, NA)

crs_warning <- NULL
display_crs_assumption <- NULL
if (crs(r) == "") {
  crs_warning <- "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
  display_crs_assumption <- "EPSG:4326"
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
}

e <- ext(r)
bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
  e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(r))
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_vect)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("band math footprint")),
    geometry = list(type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"), coordinates = list(footprint_coords))
  ))
)

vals <- values(result, mat = FALSE)
valid <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
has_valid <- length(valid) > 0

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(as.numeric(ifelse(is.finite(vals), vals, NaN)), con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
data_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)), height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)), data = jsonlite::unbox(data_b64),
  wgs84Bounds = round(c(e$xmin, e$ymin, e$xmax, e$ymax), 6),
  crs = NULL, crsWarning = jsonlite::unbox(crs_warning),
  displayCrsAssumption = jsonlite::unbox(display_crs_assumption),
  min = if (has_valid) jsonlite::unbox(round(min(valid), 4)) else NULL,
  max = if (has_valid) jsonlite::unbox(round(max(valid), 4)) else NULL,
  mean = if (has_valid) jsonlite::unbox(round(mean(valid), 4)) else NULL,
  nodataCount = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals) - length(valid)), totalPixels = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals))
)

result_out <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)`
```

## 7. Where to next

- **Just needed the computed raster?** The
  [standalone Raster Calculator](/tools/raster-calculator.html) picks
  bands and an operator from a dropdown, no editing required.
- **Not sure what's in the file yet?** Start with
  [Raster Inspector](/tools/raster-inspector.html) — dimensions,
  bands, CRS, NoData, before computing anything.
- **Working with vector data instead?** See
  [First Look at a Geospatial File](geospatial-file-inspection.qmd).
- **Vegetation index specifically?** See
  [NDVI: Measuring Vegetation from Two Bands](raster-ndvi.qmd), or the
  standalone [NDVI Calculator](/tools/ndvi-calculator.html) — this
  same Normalized Difference operation, with red/near-infrared band
  presets and a vegetation color scale.
